hypothesis: PACT produces narrower useful PIs for pediatric drug-outcome rates with reliable empirical coverage, especially under sparse pediatric evidence.

selective_secondary.reason: Original primary abstention MAE equals disagreement MAE (1.188) for all methods; width-abstention 0.944 is secondary and partly reflects adaptive widths vs constant global width.

notes: Final-test reuse is exploratory for new claims; reproduction audit confirms original numbers.

Empirically matched coverage on final-test is DESCRIPTIVE ONLY.
Primary cal-selected competitor is B7_indiv_scale (normalized conformal with same scale features; no locality).
PACT vs B7 at nominal 90%: width Delta=-0.136 (95% CI [-0.185,-0.085]); statistically significant but does NOT meet prespecified meaningful threshold (CI entirely < -0.10).
Repeated splits: PACT width 4.974+/-0.138 vs B7 4.998+/-0.125 — practically tied; locality adds little beyond individualized scale.
DESCRIPTIVE matched-cov widths identical for PACT/B7/B8 (5.107) because they share the same sigma-hat; global matched 5.652.
Width-abstention MAE@50%: B7 0.927 vs PACT 0.944 — individualized scale alone matches/beats PACT ranking; do not claim PACT-specific selective gain.
vs Global (not primary competitor): clear width advantage Delta=-0.832 CI entirely below -0.10 with coverage still in [0.85,0.95].
honest_summary: PACT reproduces and maintains ~nominal coverage with narrower intervals than global/Mondrian/denom baselines. Against the strongest fair baseline (individualized residual-scale conformal, B7), the remaining locality-driven width gain is small, not protocol-meaningful, and nearly absent across repeated splits. Selective primary ranking was disagreement-tied (not PACT-specific). No independent pediatric CT cohort. Suitable as a careful empirical workshop study, not a method-paper claim of new guarantees.
